Bridgend's population increased by around 6,300 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 150,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Bridgend increased by 4.5%, from just under 139,200 in 2011 to around 145,500 in 2021.

This means Bridgend's population saw the third-greatest increase in Wales, behind Newport (where the population increased by 9.5%) and Cardiff (4.7%). The population of Wales increased by 1.4%, from 3,063,000 to 3,107,000.

In 2021, Bridgend was home to around 4.1 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 4.0 in 2011. This area was the seventh most densely populated out of all 22 local authority areas across Wales.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Bridgend than across Wales

An older Bridgend

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Bridgend increased by two years, from 41 to 43 years of age.

This area had a slightly higher average (median) age than nearby Neath Port Talbot (43 years) and a slightly higher average (median) age than Wales as a whole (42 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 3,500 (an increase of 13.0%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 3,500 (11.6% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.6 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Change in number of Welsh language speakers

The percentage of Welsh speakers in Bridgend fell from 9.7% in 2011 to 9.2% in 2021.

In 2021, there were just under 70 fewer Welsh-speaking Bridgend residents (over the age of three years) compared with 2011. The number of people who did not speak Welsh increased by 6,800.

In nearby Neath Port Talbot, 13.5% of people over the age of three years could speak Welsh, down from 15.3% at the 2011 Census. Across Wales, the percentage of Welsh speakers fell from 19.0% to 17.8%.

Cardiff was one of the few areas that saw an increase in the percentage of Welsh speakers (from 11.1% in 2011 to 12.2% in 2021), while Carmarthenshire saw the largest fall (from 43.9% to 39.9%).

The percentage of people who could speak Welsh in Bridgend decreased by 0.5 percentage points

Health in Bridgend

In 2021, 46.3% of Bridgend residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 45.1% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" rose from 30.0% to 31.8%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Bridgend residents describing their health as "very bad" decreased from 2.2% to 1.8%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 7.0% to 5.5%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in bad health in Bridgend decreased by 1.5 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Of Bridgend households, 15.3% rented privately in 2021, up from 12.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in seven households (13.9%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 13.8% in 2011. The percentage of Bridgend households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 72.4% to 70.5%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in nearby Neath Port Talbot (3.6 percentage points) than in Bridgend (3.0 percentage points). In nearby Neath Port Talbot, the percentage increased from 10.2% in 2011 to 13.9% in 2021, while across Wales, the percentage increased from 14.1% to 17.0%.

Private renting in Bridgend increased by 3.0 percentage points

Disability in Bridgend

In 2021, 11.0% of Bridgend residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 14.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over one in nine people (11.3%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 11.6% in 2011. The proportion of Bridgend residents who were not disabled increased from 74.4% to 77.7%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Bridgend (3.1 percentage points) was similar to the decrease in nearby Neath Port Talbot (3.3 percentage points). In nearby Neath Port Talbot, the proportion fell from 16.2% in 2011 to 12.9% in 2021, while across Wales, the proportion fell from 12.3% to 10.0%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Bridgend decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Unpaid care in Bridgend

In 2021, 4.6% of Bridgend residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.3% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, around 1 in 40 people (2.5%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 2.1% in 2011. The proportion of Bridgend residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care decreased from 4.3% to 4.0%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Bridgend (2.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease in nearby Neath Port Talbot (3.0 percentage points). In nearby Neath Port Talbot, the proportion fell from 7.8% in 2011 to 4.8% in 2021, while across Wales, the proportion fell from 7.4% to 4.7%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Bridgend decreased by 2.7 percentage points

Religion in Bridgend

In 2021, 52.3% of Bridgend residents reported having "No religion", making it the most common response in this local authority area (up from 36.7% in 2011). Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across Wales, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 32.1% to 46.5%.

In 2021, 40.4% of people in Bridgend described themselves as Christian (down from 55.1%), while 5.6% did not state their religion (down from 7.0% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 52.3% of usual residents in Bridgend reported having "No religion"

Bridgend residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 119,300 Bridgend residents said they were born in Wales. This represented 82.0% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 115,700 in 2011, which at the time represented 83.1% of Bridgend's population.

England was the next most represented, with around 18,500 Bridgend residents reporting this country of birth (12.7%). This figure was up from around 17,000 in 2011, which at the time represented 12.2% of the population of Bridgend.

The number of Bridgend residents born in Scotland remained close to 1,100 between the last two census (from 0.8% of the local population in 2011 to 0.7% in 2021)

In 2021, 82.0% of Bridgend residents reported their country of birth as Wales

National identity in Bridgend

Of Bridgend residents, 64.8% identified as "Welsh" (and no other national identity) in 2021, down from 67.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 11 people (9.4%) described themselves as "Welsh and British only", compared with 8.5% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Bridgend that identified as "British only" increased from 13.4% to 15.0%.

The decrease in the percentage of people who identified as "Welsh only" was greater in nearby Neath Port Talbot (3.5 percentage points) than in Bridgend (2.5 percentage points). In nearby Neath Port Talbot, the percentage fell from 71.8% in 2011 to 68.3% in 2021, while across Wales, the percentage fell from 57.5% to 55.2%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who identified as "Welsh only" in Bridgend decreased by 2.5 percentage points

Family in Bridgend

Of Bridgend households, 17.0% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 18.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in six households (17.9%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 19.5% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children decreased from 7.8% to 7.5%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in nearby Neath Port Talbot (1.4 percentage points) than in Bridgend (1.0 percentage points). In nearby Neath Port Talbot, the percentage fell from 16.8% in 2011 to 15.4% in 2021, while across Wales, the percentage fell from 17.2% to 16.5%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Bridgend decreased by 1.0 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Bridgend residents aged 16 years and over, 35.1% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 30.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (45.3%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 48.8% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Bridgend that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership remained at 10.4%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in nearby Neath Port Talbot (5.4 percentage points) than in Bridgend (4.2 percentage points). In nearby Neath Port Talbot, the percentage increased from 31.2% in 2011 to 36.6% in 2021, while across Wales, the percentage increased from 33.5% to 37.2%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Bridgend increased by 4.2 percentage points

Employment in Bridgend

Of Bridgend residents aged 16 years and over, 52.4% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, the same percentage as in 2011.

In 2021, around 1 in 40 people (2.5%) said they were unemployed, compared with 4.1% in 2011. The percentage of retired Bridgend residents increased from 24.1% to 24.7%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed fell from 49.9% to 49.2% in nearby Neath Port Talbot. Across Wales, the percentage fell from 52.5% to 51.9%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

In 2021, 52.4% of usual residents aged 16 years and over said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in Bridgend

Change in work hours

In 2021, 7.9% of Bridgend residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure decreased from 8.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 11 people (9.3%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 10.6% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 60.0% to 62.8%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was 8.0% (similar to 2011) in nearby Neath Port Talbot. Across Wales, the percentage fell from 9.3% to 9.0%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Bridgend decreased by 0.4 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Bridgend

In 2021, 1.5% of Bridgend residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 1.1% in 2011. The 0.4 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across Wales, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 2.3% to 2.9%.

In 2021, 96.8% of people in Bridgend identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 97.8% in 2011), while 1.2% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 0.7% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.2% in 2011 to 0.3% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
